items.headline: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
items.blurb: The new levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, including China and the EU.
items.text: The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as President Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy. The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of the country's biggest trading partners - China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions. The move follows the White House's investigation into the trade practices of other countries in March after the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's previously announced Liberation Day tariffs were illegal . China is facing the highest rate of up to 40%, followed by Vietnam at up to 35% and then others facing either 20% or 25%. The new duties are not expected to take effect until next year. Tariffs are taxes levied on imported goods. The amount is typically calculated as a percentage of the good's value and paid to the government by businesses importing the products from abroad. Some of these rates will be effectively reduced because of caps on tariffs Trump has agreed to. Individual countries also face different levies. The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the public prosecutor’s office said in a statement. The stretch of the highway where the crash occurred was in Waraq, a densely populated neighbourhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, according to the health ministry. At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video showed firefighters working to put out the fire spreading among the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb. The Egyptian president, Abdel-Fattah al-Sissi , expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. items.headline: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater
items.blurb: The asteroid's surface was transformed after a spacecraft was deliberately crashed into it four years ago
items.text: The first images of an asteroid that Nasa deliberately crashed into have revealed a stadium-sized crater on its surface. The extensive damage was caused when a Nasa spacecraft hit the asteroid Dimorphos in 2022. The asteroid posed no threat, but this was a test of our planetary defences to see if it was possible to knock a space rock off course. Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) spacecraft called Hera is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision. "The crater is almost as large as the body itself, which is really, really spectacular," said Dr Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist, who is on the Hera science team. "It's hard to describe in words all the excitement to actually finally see what happened. And as a crater person, I can also say it's beautiful." The original 2022 crash test was carried out by a Nasa spacecraft called Dart which hurtled into Dimorphos at 14,000mph (22,000km/h). The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports. items.blurb: Another 21 are injured after the tanker reportedly overturns on a busy ring road in the Egyptian capital.
items.text: Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says. Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening. Unverified footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched. Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the tanker had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol. The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead. The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation. items.headline: Storms push Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City to Saturday
items.blurb: The parade, which marks its 100th edition, got a last-minute rain check ahead of heavy gusts on Thursday.
items.text: New York City is famous for its annual Thanksgiving Day Parade, a procession of towering helium balloons, elaborate floats and marching bands. But on Wednesday, organisers in the United States announced that this year’s edition has been postponed because of an East Coast storm that threatens turbulent weather. It was rescheduled for Saturday instead, right after Black Friday, a day when retailers traditionally offer holiday shopping and discount prices. The annual parade is sponsored by Macy’s, a New York-based department store brand, and Saturday’s event will be its 100th Thanksgiving procession. “While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our participants and spectators is and always will be our top priority,” Will Coss, Macy’s executive producer, said in a Wednesday news conference. “ We’re saddened by the shift, but we’re optimistic about our opportunity to deliver the most spectacular 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, the best and biggest parade in our history.” The parade, founded in 1924, was cancelled three times during World War II, but this year marks the first time it was postponed. items.headline: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
items.blurb: The Israeli PM says his trial should end after judges said there was little chance of conviction in one of three cases.
items.text: Judges in Israel have suggested prosecutors drop bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu, potentially handing the caretaker prime minister a boost as he fights for his political survival. The judges told the attorney general that there was little chance of conviction in the first of three cases he is facing, in which he is accused of granting government favours in exchange for positive media coverage. They also questioned whether his actions amounted to criminal conduct in a second corruption case, and suggested prosecutors seek a plea deal in a third. Netanyahu has consistently denied the allegations against him and called on Wednesday for the trial to be ended "immediately". "Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my family, my son," he said in a televised statement. Netanyahu was first charged in 2019, but court proceedings have been prolonged in part by the recent Israel-Gaza war. The case now under serious doubt, known as Case 4,000, concerns an alleged "reciprocal arrangement" between Netanyahu and the controlling shareholder in Israel's biggest telecoms company. While pointing out the potential of India’s private space companies, the autonomous body under the Department of Space underlined the challenges ahead. items.text: Amid reported friction between the Samajwadi Party and Congress ahead of the 2027 assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, Congress MP Imran Masood has not ruled out a possible alliance with Bahujan Samaj party on Wednesday. However, the Congress MP added that BSP chief Mayawati would have to be the one to take the initiative to form an alliance. "We haven't even held any discussions yet. I have always maintained that all like-minded people, those who wish to uphold the banner of secularism, should come together. But Behenji (Mayawati) would have to step forward, and she simply doesn't, does she?" Masood was quoted as saying by news agency ANI. At present, the Bahujan Samaj Party is contesting the UP election solo. For the assembly elections, apart from the SP-Congress alliance, AIMIM's Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram)'s Chandrashekar Azad have also formed an alliance. items.text: A suspected cattle smuggler died while three others got injured after the car they were escaping in the wrong direction to avoid police, collided head-on with a truck on the Kundli-Manesar-Palwal (KMP) Expressway in Nuh on Wednesday, police said on Thursday. One of the two cattle being smuggled in the car also died in the accident, police said, adding the other survived. Krishan Kumar, public relations officer of Nuh police, said the car collided with an oncoming truck near Goyla village, leaving all four occupants injured. “All the injured suspects were rushed to different hospitals. Mustafa, however, succumbed to his injuries in the course of treatment,” he said. Kumar said a first information report (FIR) was registered against the suspects at Mohammadpur Ahir police station under various provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Haryana Gauvansh Sanrakshan and Gau Samvardhan Act. The victim was identified as Mohammad Mustafa, a resident of Palla in Faridabad. Those injured were Mohammad Akhlaq and Asif, who were also from Palla and Mohammad Iqbal from Mankaki, Palwal. items.headline: Beyond 26/11: Other major terror attacks in Mumbai over the years
items.blurb: Here is a look at some of the other major terror attacks that have struck Mumbai city over the years, apart from the 26/11 attacks
items.text: Smoke is seen billowing out of the ground and first floor of the Taj Hotel in south Mumbai during security personnel’s “Operation Cyclone” following the 26/11 terror attacks in 2008. File photo | Photo Credit: PTI On November 26, 2008, 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorists from Pakistan arrived by sea and killed 166 people, including 18 security personnel, besides injuring more than 300 others during a 60-hour siege of Mumbai. The terrorists targeted several high-profile locations, including the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, the Oberoi Trident, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus and Nariman House. But the city has been rattled by other attacks too, including the horrific 1993 Mumbai blasts. As Mumbai marks the anniversary of the 26/11 attacks, here is a look at some of the other major terror attacks that have struck the city over the years. On March 12, 1993, 13 coordinated serial blasts ripped through Mumbai’s commercial and social hubs, killing 257 people and injuring more than 700. items.headline: Lajja Gauri idol to Tagore painting: Yuge Yugeen museum takes shape
items.blurb: The gallery will be the first of seven themed galleries planned across the North and South Blocks, with the larger museum expected to display 1.8 m objects.
items.text: A section of Delhi’s North Bloc k, once home to key government ministries including Home and Finance, will open to the public towards the end of 2027 as part of the government’s Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum, with its first gallery showcasing up to 1,000 objects tracing India’s traditions of adornment. The gallery will be the first of seven themed galleries planned across the North and South Blocks, with the larger museum expected to display 1.8 million objects. Other themes include Mathematics and Astronomy, Architecture and Cityscapes, Healing Systems and Medicine, Beliefs and Spirituality, Languages and Scripts, and Bharat Connects -Trade and Ideas. The exhibits will be sourced from government museums across the country, including the Kolkata-based Indian Museum, the country’s oldest museum. A dedicated team has been appointed to examine collections and select objects for the galleries. For the Adornment gallery, the Indian Museum has sent rare works, including a Mauryan period stone sculpture of the Earth goddess, called the Lajja Gauri figure, and a 14th century statue of Darpanika (Surasundari) from the Eastern Ganga Dynasty from Puri, Odisha. items.blurb: SpaceX has secured FCC approval to deploy 1 million orbital compute modules for data centres in space. The project, dubbed Starmind, aims to harness solar power but faces concerns over satellite collisions, atmospheric pollution and night-sky pollution.
items.text: Elon Musk's SpaceX has received authorisation from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) in the United States to deploy up to 1 million orbital compute modules as part of a plan to build data centres in space. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, in a statement on Wednesday, said the decision "opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth". He added that the United States was already leading the world into the era of super intelligence and was moving "decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people". "The Starmind & competitor constellations will use solar power to extend America's lead in Super Intelligence," Carr wrote in a post on X. Responding to Carr's post, Musk said, "Much appreciated. This will be a great asset to America and the world." According to a CNBC report citing the FCC's authorisation filing, SpaceX 's application attracted a substantial number of public comments, including petitions seeking to block the project from Kuiper Systems LLC (Amazon Leo), Viasat Inc.

items.blurb: Situational Awareness told investors it lost 65% after fees in the third quarter, after highly levered bets on artificial intelligence firms nearly led to the hedge fund’s implosion in July, according to the Wall Street Journal.
items.text: (Bloomberg) -- Situational Awareness told investors it lost 65% after fees in the third quarter, after highly levered bets on artificial intelligence firms nearly led to the hedge fund’s implosion in July, according to the Wall Street Journal. The hedge fund is still up 88.5% after fees for the year through the month of September, founder Leopold Aschenbrenner said in a letter viewed by the Wall Street Journal. Despite the tumult, the fund stills sees opportunities to invest with high potential for return, according to the report. Situational Awareness was pushed to the brink in July as a brief moment of panic about AI spread across global markets, sparking margin calls from banks and turning it into a symbol of the wild swings that have accompanied the AI trade. The firm ultimately sold a large chunk of its public equities portfolio to Ken Griffin’s Citadel. items.headline: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk
items.blurb: The discount chain has fallen into administration after its owners failed to find a buyer.
items.text: Poundland has collapsed into administration, putting 11,000 jobs at risk, after its owners failed to find a buyer to keep it in business. The retailer's shops and distribution centres will remain open and continue to trade during the administration process with the business likely to be broken up and some of its stores sold off to rival retailers. Poundland's US owners held talks with several bidders over a last-minute rescue deal, but no agreement was reached. Poundland boss Barry Williams said in a note to staff that the board had "no alternative but to take this decision", but was making it with "sincere sadness and intense regret". He said the US owners Gordon Brothers had removed "all borrowing facilities and access to our bank accounts" on 27 October, and adequate funds had not been released since then to keep the business solvent. "Under these circumstances, it is impossible for the board of directors to see how Poundland can continue to operate as a going concern," he added. The details of the investigation emerged after Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO after he had resigned over claims of extramarital affairs, one with Alice Huang, a suspected "Chinese spy." However, US authorities previously said that they do not possess any evidence of Alice Huang being directed by Chinese intelligence to spy on the Nvidia founder. The latest investigation by the CBS News raises concerns over efforts to prevent sensitive technology from reaching countries considered rivals of the US. According to the CBS News investigation, one of Nvidia's "preferred partners" is a California-based company owned by a Chinese firm. items.text: Zostel has approached the Delhi High Court seeking to revive its claim to a 7% stake in Oravel Stays, OYO's parent company, as it moves towards a proposed IPO. The company has challenged a May 2025 order that set aside a 2021 arbitral award recognising its entitlement to the stake following a proposed acquisition of its hotel aggregation business, Zo Rooms, in 2015. During Wednesday's hearing, Zostel argued that the court should have set aside only the relief granted by the arbitrator rather than the entire award. It maintained that the tribunal's findings on the binding nature of the deal and Oravel's alleged breach should have been retained. The dispute dates back to November 2015, when Oravel and Zostel signed a term sheet for the acquisition of Zo Rooms. Under the proposed deal, Zostel's shareholders were to receive a 7% stake in Oravel. Although the term sheet was described as non-binding, Zostel argued that subsequent actions by both parties made it binding. The final agreements were never signed. items.headline: Orthopaedic healthcare startup OSSO raises Rs 2.5 Cr in extended seed round
items.blurb: Gurugram-based orthopaedic healthcare startup OSSO has raised Rs 2.5 crore as part of its extended seed funding round. The company will use the fresh capital to expand its clinical capabilities and presence across the National Capital Region (NCR), OSSO said in a press release.
items.text: Gurugram-based orthopaedic healthcare startup OSSO has raised Rs 2.5 crore as part of its extended seed funding round. The company will use the fresh capital to expand its clinical capabilities and presence across the National Capital Region (NCR), OSSO said in a press release. The extended round saw participation from Rajeev Saraf, Tejinderpal Miglani, Priyanka Aggarwal, Akshay Varma and Vikas Bhadoria. They join existing investors, including Umesh Kumar Agarwal from the Haldiram Family Office, Sahil Jindal and Blume Founders Fund, among others. Founded in 2025 by Kunal Kishore Dhawan and Avani Shukla, OSSO operates an integrated orthopaedic and rehabilitation centre that combines clinical orthopaedics, physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R), physiotherapy, regenerative orthopaedics and sports injury care. The startup's newly launched centre will focus on advanced orthopaedic procedures, particularly joint preservation and sports injury treatment. The facility will offer procedures such as image-guided orthobiologic interventions, subchondral bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC) and arthroscopic cartilage repair. Several of these treatments are minimally invasive and can be performed as day-care procedures. The new centre will operate alongside OSSO's flagship clinic in DLF Phase

items.headline: AI is straining America’s open records systems
items.blurb: In Panton, Vermont, population 660, town clerk Kyle Rowe did it all. He crafted budgets, paid vendors, handled property tax disputes, and served as the town’s zoning supervisor and presiding elections officer.
items.text: In Panton, Vermont, population 660, town clerk Kyle Rowe did it all. He crafted budgets, paid vendors, handled property tax disputes, and served as the town’s zoning supervisor and presiding elections officer. During morning office hours at the town hall—a wood-frame structure built as a church in 1858—he also fielded public records requests. Recently, he got rather busy. Panton used to get a request every year or so from a company called SmartProcure for “all purchasing records,” covering everything from road salt to computers to toilet paper. Last year, those requests started coming quarterly. Then different companies began making more specific requests, like records of every purchase related to emergency road flares. These targeted inquiries started coming monthly or more. “I’m happy to answer public records requests from people,” says Rowe, who recently moved into a position at a nearby town. “But answering it for these purposes—it feels like I’m doing unpaid opposition research on the taxpayers’ time.” Rowe’s experiences are being repeated across the US. While data brokers have mined public records for decades, AI has intensified investors’ interest.

items.headline: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
items.blurb: Frontier AI is already solving problems that once took top physicists a full day.
items.text: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics. LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online. The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI. items.text: Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility more seriously than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well. Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm. This thinking isn’t all that fringe. items.headline: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
items.blurb: A new AI-assisted proof seems to be solid, but we're not sure what it tells us.
items.text: Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis . The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset. It’s too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math. The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There’s not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. items.headline: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.blurb: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.
items.text: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled. The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. items.headline: S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and ‘key man’ risks
items.blurb: The credit rating agency may lower Nvidia's credit rating to AA-, the fourth-highest rating.
items.text: S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the company’s management and governance practices. Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement . The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale. Although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral. In August, Nvidia announced plans to arrange $500 billion in financing for AI infrastructure with six financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone. In an announcement on Wednesday , the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company’s “Starmind” initiative . With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space , including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full “constellation” of AI satellites. The FCC’s approval requires SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033, and meet the 1 million satellite milestone by 2040. The FCC also deferred SpaceX’s request to dispose of satellites located above 600km in space “graveyard” orbits , rather than having them burn up in the Earth’s atmosphere, saying the company hasn’t provided “sufficient information” about its disposal process plans. items.headline: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia’s code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
items.blurb: Most codes of conduct serve as a reflection of corporate culture. In Nvidia's case, that could have consequences.
items.text: When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired . “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO. It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. items.text: ⁠Nvidia has made clear⁠ it won’t backstop an AI data center until it’s nearly ready to run, and that’s landing just as neoclouds report construction delays and more expensive debt. The message to developers is that land, power, and a finished building matter more than a pitch deck. ⁠Anita Verma-Lallian⁠ has been selling exactly that. Her company, Arizona Land Consulting, assembles data center sites for developers, hyperscalers, AI labs, and neoclouds, giving her a view into who’s buying, what makes a site viable, and where projects are running into trouble. She also partners with investor ⁠Chamath Palihapitiya,⁠ who has been predicting an industry shakeout. On this episode of TechCrunch’s ⁠Equity⁠ podcast, Rebecca Bellan talks with Verma-Lallian about who bears the risk when Nvidia gets pickier, why speculative projects could be the first to fall apart, and what a 2027 shakeout might look like. items.headline: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
items.blurb: AI songs account for 6.3 percent of Tidal's catalog, but it's about to be zero.
items.text: Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists. Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn’t enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated. As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal’s total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. items.text: On Monday morning, Jensen Huang walked into Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters to rapturous applause from employees lining the walkways above him. Huang was visibly moved as one colleague threw themselves into his arms for a hug. The spectacular reinstatement of the chief executive of Nvidia, less than two weeks after he resigned in a scandal over an affair with a customer and suspected Chinese spy—as well as a second reported affair with a subordinate—caught even the company’s most senior executives by surprise. The abrupt reversal by Nvidia’s board was spurred by President Donald Trump, who applied pressure to the board over the weekend after watching what was once America’s most valuable company as well as the wider tech sector haemorrhage value last week. It was the culmination of frenetic lobbying by a “war room” of Huang’s Silicon Valley allies, who pulled in Trump and vice-president JD Vance, according to people familiar with the events. items.text: Amazon may be having a change of heart about Meta’s AI agent, Muse. According to a Wednesday report by Fortune , citing people familiar with the discussions, Amazon and Meta have held multiple rounds of talks about the matter. Two key issues remain under negotiation: how search results would be presented and how advertising would be handled under a potential agreement. One of Amazon’s biggest concerns is how third-party shopping agents like Muse could affect its advertising business. items.text: Sarvam AI has expanded its product portfolio with an upgraded 105B large language model and Dictate, a speech-to-text API supporting English and 22 Indian languages Beyond building sovereign AI models, Sarvam is looking to become a one-stop shop for enterprise AI in India, offering everything from foundation models and inference infrastructure to AI-powered applications While its upgraded 105B model narrows the performance gap with global peers on conversational tasks, its voice AI business is already finding commercial traction, clocking over 3 Mn minutes a day and a billion-plus API calls a month, according to the company Last week, Sarvam AI found itself in the eye of a storm . The poster child of India’s sovereign AI ambitions drew flak for offering access to Chinese AI models, including DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM, through its newly launched inference platform, Token Factory. The point of contention among critics has been whether a startup that received government support to build indigenous AI models should be in the business of selling access to Chinese models. items.headline: What Jensen Huang’s NVIDIA Return Means For India’s AI Players
items.blurb: Jensen Huang’s return as NVIDIA CEO has eased concerns over leadership continuity at a key supplier to India’s AI ecosystem.…
items.text: Huang’s return brings greater leadership certainty, but is unlikely to immediately improve GPU availability, lower procurement costs for Indian operators Indian AI companies’ dependence on NVIDIA’s hardware and software leaves them exposed to changes in its supply priorities, global demand, and US export policies NVIDIA accounts for 81.6% of compute units listed on the IndiaAI Compute Portal. Analysts recommend diversifying suppliers, improving infrastructure utilisation Jensen Huang’s return as NVIDIA CEO has eased concerns over leadership continuity at a key supplier to India’s AI ecosystem. However, analysts say it does little to address the Indian AI ecosystem’s dependence on the chipmaker or the constraints keeping advanced computing infrastructure expensive. NVIDIA announced Huang’s reinstatement on November 23, following his resignation on November 12. US President Donald Trump welcomed the decision, describing Huang as a “national treasure”. His departure had raised questions about NVIDIA’s investment plans, supply-chain management, pace of product innovation, and ability to retain talent.
